questions.stem: An organism that manufactures its own organic food from simple inorganic substances is described as
questions.explanation: Autotrophs build organic molecules such as glucose from carbon dioxide and water, using either light energy (photosynthesis) or energy from chemical reactions (chemosynthesis). All other modes listed depend on organic food that another organism has already made.

distractorRationale.a: Heterotrophs depend on ready-made organic food
distractorRationale.c: Saprophytes are a kind of heterotroph that feeds on dead organic matter
distractorRationale.d: Parasites are heterotrophs that take food from a living host

questions.stem: Rhizopus growing on stale bread secretes enzymes onto the bread and absorbs the digested products. This mode of nutrition is
questions.explanation: The bread is dead organic matter and digestion happens outside the fungus before absorption, which is exactly what defines saprophytic nutrition. Saprophytes are the decomposers that release nutrients back into the soil.

distractorRationale.a: Holozoic feeders take solid food into a gut and digest it internally
distractorRationale.b: A parasite feeds on a living host and harms it; bread is not alive
distractorRationale.d: Chemosynthesis is a form of autotrophic nutrition, and Rhizopus makes no food of its own

questions.stem: Rhizobium bacteria live in the root nodules of cowpea. The bacteria supply the plant with fixed nitrogen and receive carbohydrates in return. This relationship is
questions.explanation: Both partners gain: the plant obtains nitrogen compounds it could not make from atmospheric nitrogen, and the bacteria obtain sugars from photosynthesis. Mutual benefit with neither partner harmed is the definition of symbiosis, and it is why legumes improve soil fertility.

distractorRationale.a: In parasitism one partner is harmed, but the cowpea benefits
distractorRationale.c: Saprophytism involves feeding on dead matter, and the root is alive
distractorRationale.d: Predation involves killing and eating another organism

questions.stem: Which deficiency disease results from a lack of iodine in the diet?
questions.explanation: Iodine is needed by the thyroid gland to manufacture thyroxine. Without it the gland enlarges as it works harder, producing the visible neck swelling called goitre; this is why table salt is iodised.

distractorRationale.b: Rickets is caused by a shortage of vitamin D or calcium
distractorRationale.c: Scurvy is caused by a shortage of vitamin C
distractorRationale.d: Beriberi is caused by a shortage of vitamin B1, thiamine

questions.stem: A two-year-old child fed almost entirely on garri and pap has a swollen abdomen, wasted limbs and discoloured hair. The most appropriate correction to the diet is to add
questions.explanation: The symptoms describe kwashiorkor, which arises when energy intake is adequate but protein is severely lacking. Beans, groundnut and crayfish are affordable local protein sources that supply the amino acids needed to rebuild tissue and correct the oedema.

distractorRationale.a: Garri and rice are starchy foods; adding more repeats the very imbalance that caused the disease
distractorRationale.c: Palm oil supplies energy and vitamin A but almost no protein
distractorRationale.d: Iodised salt prevents goitre, which is a different deficiency

questions.stem: Roughage is an important part of the diet even though it is not digested. Its main function is to

options.text: add bulk that stimulates peristalsis and prevents constipation
form haemoglobin in red blood cells

questions.explanation: Roughage is mainly cellulose, which human enzymes cannot break down. It stays in the gut as bulk that the muscular wall can grip, keeping peristalsis regular so that faeces pass out easily.

distractorRationale.a: Humans cannot digest cellulose, so no energy is obtained from it
distractorRationale.b: Amino acids come from protein, not from fibre
distractorRationale.d: Haemoglobin formation requires iron and protein

questions.stem: A pitcher plant that traps and digests insects should be classified as a heterotroph.
questions.explanation: False. The pitcher plant is green and makes all its own carbohydrate by photosynthesis, so it is an autotroph. It digests insects only to obtain nitrogen and mineral salts, which are scarce in the marshy soils where it grows.

questions.stem: A farmer complains that he cannot see clearly at dusk although his daytime vision is normal. Which food should be added to his diet?

options.text: Red palm oil and dark green leafy vegetables

questions.explanation: Poor vision in dim light is night blindness, caused by a shortage of vitamin A, which the retina needs to make the pigment rhodopsin. Red palm oil and dark green leaves are rich in carotene, which the body converts to vitamin A.

distractorRationale.a: Citrus fruits supply vitamin C, which prevents scurvy rather than night blindness
distractorRationale.c: Rice and cassava are energy foods with negligible vitamin A
distractorRationale.d: Sugar supplies energy only and contains no vitamins

questions.stem: Mistletoe grows on the branches of a cocoa tree, has green leaves of its own but sends root-like structures into the host's xylem. It is best described as
questions.explanation: Because it is green it photosynthesises and makes its own carbohydrate, but it taps the host's xylem for water and mineral salts, which harms the host. Depending on the host for only some requirements makes it a partial, or semi, parasite.

distractorRationale.a: A complete parasite such as dodder has no chlorophyll and takes everything from the host
distractorRationale.c: A saprophyte feeds on dead matter, whereas the cocoa tree is alive
distractorRationale.d: In symbiosis both partners benefit, but the cocoa tree is damaged

questions.stem: Explain what is meant by a balanced diet and state, with reasons, two ways in which the diet of a pregnant woman should differ from that of an office clerk of the same age.
markingGuide: Balanced diet defined as one containing all the food classes — carbohydrate, protein, fat, vitamins, mineral salts, water and roughage — in the correct proportions for the individual's age, sex, body size and occupation (3 marks)
Difference 1: more protein, because amino acids are needed to build the tissues of the developing foetus as well as maintain the mother (2 marks)
Difference 2: more calcium and vitamin D for the bones and teeth of the foetus, or more iron to make the extra haemoglobin required by the increased blood volume and to prevent anaemia (2 marks)
Reason correctly linked to the nutrient in each case rather than merely naming the nutrient (1 mark)
questions.explanation: A balanced diet is defined by proportion as well as by content, which is why requirements differ between individuals. Pregnancy raises the demand for protein for foetal tissue growth and for iron and calcium to support the increased blood volume and skeletal development of the foetus.
